Labflow: research, competitive comparison and go-live scope

Reviewed14–15 November2026 for a laboratory in India targeting approximately100 patients/day. Public vendor pages and operational documentation were reviewed; no commercial product was installed or benchmarked. Advertised features are not independently established reliability, clinical validity, contractual availability or certification. “Not established” means the cited pages did not demonstrate a detail.

Primary sources

1. CrelioHealth laboratory testing: specimen custody, instruments, report validation, critical findings and delivery.

2. CrelioHealth QC help: reviewer decisions on incoming control results; configuration is required.

3. MocDoc LIMS: barcode lifecycle, machine transfer, delta checks, approval, dispatch and multiple sites.

4. Labsmart reporting and employee accountability: configurable reports/reference data, staff permissions, activity history and sharing.

5. SENAITE features: state-aware roles, independent verification, quality controls, instrument state and PDF publication. It is a broader laboratory LIMS; clinical patient-workflow equivalence is not assumed.

6. MeitY DPDP rules and enforcement documents and NABL medical laboratories: official Indian references for the lab’s legal/quality review. DPDP commencement is staged. The lab needs advice for its actual obligations and dates; software features do not create NABL accreditation.

Compared capabilities

Report generationLabsmart: configurable forms, intervals and sharing; others: validation/publishing15 starter panels,3 styles, snapshots of released values/definitions/profile, readable draft labels, structured reviewLab-approved age/sex/method intervals, real A4/PDF acceptance, narrative/microbiology panels, corrected report versions
Staff authorityCrelio/MocDoc: roles and audit; SENAITE: independent verificationNamed scrypt-backed accounts, six roles, revocable protected sessions; independent entry/release identities by defaultInstitutional onboarding, MFA/SSO, formal staff qualification review, external security assessment
Specimen traceabilityCrelio/MocDoc: barcode lifecycle; SENAITE: sample identifiers/workflowSeparate specimen IDs, fasting/postprandial split, Code39 labels, collect/receive/reject/recollect and replacement IDsActual scanner/stock/printer validation, custody across couriers/branches, aliquot/archival lifecycle
QC and critical resultsCrelio help: reviewed controls; SENAITE: controls/instrument-state gatesRecorded QC evidence with expiry/hold; only configured critical rules; real notification/read-back tied to result revisionLab-specific critical thresholds, quality policies, QC charting/calibration, instrument acceptance
Analyzer ingestionCrelio/MocDoc: instrument interfacesAtomic mapped CSV drafts, exact units or explicit conversion, provenance, replay protection, no automatic releaseEach actual model/protocol, serial/TCP/ASTM/HL7 middleware, real acceptance files. Universal compatibility is not established
Report deliveryCrelio/MocDoc/Labsmart: channel delivery and trackingRecipient consent plus durable idempotent delivery requests; explicitly blocked when no providerActual WhatsApp/email accounts, approved templates, secure patient links, transport retries and authenticated receipts
RecoveryCommercial pages advertise hosting/recovery; operational detail variesConsistent full SQLite backup encrypted AES-256-GCM; actual restore/integrity tests and revoked restored sessionsOff-site storage, recovery-key custody, scheduled monitored jobs, documented operator restore drill and RPO/RTO
Scale and multiple sitesMocDoc/Crelio describe branch operationsOne server with persistent local SQLite, bounded initial worklists, full-database search, tested100-order concurrent workflowLong-term retention/representative peak pilot, multi-branch tenancy/transfers and horizontal scaling

The useful competitive position is a focused, transparent reporting workflow with testable controls and a small self-hosted footprint. The evidence does not establish that Labflow surpasses established systems, has full feature parity, or is ready to process clinical data without local acceptance.

Engineering work delivered

The earlier shared administrator/browser-demo model has been separated from the real server deployment. Staff roles, review separation, specimen records, quality gates, instrument import validation, blocked delivery intents, full-database backup/restore, deployment checks and regression coverage are implemented in the source package. The live private Sites publication is a demonstration; publishing static files does not deploy the Node/SQLite service or make its browser-local records shared.

The isolated workload completed100 fictional patients,500 clinical writes and8 concurrent requests with zero unexpected failures and100 independently approved reports. See BENCHMARK.md for exact measurements and limits. These are test results, not a production SLA.

Acceptance and rollout

1. Deploy a staging server: select the managed host, persistent encrypted disk, HTTPS origin, staff accounts, backup secret and off-site backup destination. Confirm unauthenticated/unauthorized denials, expiry/revocation, version conflicts and restore recovery.

2. Validate laboratory behavior: the qualified lab reviews catalog/methods/intervals, specimen identity, rejection/recollection, critical callbacks, control evidence, reviewer authority, printouts and scanner labels. Record exactly which software/catalog revision was tested. Check privacy notices, consent, access, retention/deletion and incident response for the actual Indian operating context.

3. Validate each connection: enumerate actual instrument models and protocols; retain accepted sample output/mapping tests. Configure delivery providers and validate failure, retry and receipt behavior. A queue entry is not a sent report.

4. Shadow pilot before clinical release: run representative orders alongside the established process, compare every result/unit/report and resolve discrepancies. Establish operational ownership, monitoring, retention, RPO/RTO and a fallback workflow. Clear readiness checks only against actual evidence.

Remaining inputs are the hosting/HTTPS choice, named lab staff and qualified reviewer, actual analyzer list/output samples, provider credentials entered through a protected secret mechanism, and lab acceptance records. No passwords or patient records should be pasted into chat or the source repository.
